question.prompt: The set of points satisfying the pair of inequalities \(y>2x\) and \(y>4-x\) is contained entirely in quadrants:

solutions.explanation:
The useful question is whether either inequality forces \(y\) to be positive. We can answer this by separating the possible signs of \(x\).

If \(x\geq 0\), then \(y>2x\geq 0\). If \(x<0\), then \(y>4-x>4\). Thus every solution has \(y>0\), so no solution lies in quadrant III or IV. Both remaining quadrants occur: \((1,5)\) satisfies both inequalities and lies in quadrant I, while \((-1,6)\) satisfies both and lies in quadrant II.

There is a wording issue at the axis. When \(x=0\), the two inequalities reduce to \(y>4\), so points such as \((0,5)\) are also solutions. Axis points belong to no quadrant. Therefore the solution set occupies quadrants I and II together with the ray \(x=0,\ y>4\). The intended choice is \(\boxed{\text{A}}\), but no listed choice is literally correct if “contained entirely” excludes axes.
